description: Create a PNG sprite from text, NES-style: 'palette' maps single characters to colors and each string in 'rows' is one row of pixels ('.' and ' ' are transparent). 'frames' (a list of row lists) makes a horizontal sprite sheet for animation. Scaled with nearest neighbour, imported immediately, undoable with edit_undo. Use the result as {"res": path} for a Sprite2D texture.

dry_run.description: Validate and report the size without writing.

frames.description: Several same-sized frames, laid out left to right. Each frame is a list of row strings: [["..##..", ...], ["..##..", ...]].

mirror.description: Symmetric sprites: give only the left half ('x'), top half ('y') or top-left quarter ('xy'); the rest is mirrored.

mirror_overlap.description: Share the middle column/row instead of repeating it (odd widths/heights).

palette.description: Character -> color ('#rrggbb', '#rrggbbaa', a name, or [r, g, b, a] in 0..1), e.g. {"k": "#000000", "r": "#d82800"}. null or 'transparent' = see-through ('.' and ' ' already are).

rows.description: One image: rows of palette characters, all the same length (max 256x256).

scale.description: Integer upscale factor (default 1). Prefer 1 and scale the node instead.

name: image_write
title: Write pixel-art PNG
